chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Fazara, from Anas or Haysam ibn al-Bara', who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The thief enters my house wanting my life and my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Kill him, and I bear witness to Allah and whoever hears it that his blood is on my neck (responsibility).'

key_terms.دَمَهُ فِي عُنُقِي: His blood is on my neck
key_terms.فَأُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ: And I bear witness to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing a thief who enters your home with intent to kill or steal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling of self-defense against an intruder with lethal intent, emphasizing that the defender is not liable for blood money (diya). The phrase 'I bear witness to God' signifies that the killing is justified and the blood is 'light' (dammun hafif), a key concept in Shia jurisprudence distinguishing it from unjust homicide. This ruling underscores the sanctity of life and property within the domestic sphere, granting the homeowner the right to use lethal force to repel immediate threat.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Qalanisy, from Ahmad Bin Al Fazl, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Farara, from Anas, or Haysam Bin Al Bara’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The thief enters into my house wanting my soul (murder me) and my wealth’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Kill, for I<sup>asws</sup> bear witness to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the one who hears that his blood is in my<sup>asws</sup> neck (responsibility)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufiy has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisiy from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Fazarah from Anas or Haytham ibn al-Bara’ who has said the following:

“I asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a thief who may enter my house to harm my life or properties.’ He (the Imam) said, ’Eliminate him. Allah and those who hear me are my witness; his blood (life) is on my neck (my responsibility).”’
